svg.aria-label: Where a uop takes and gives back its resources
svg.text: Where a uop takes and gives back its resources
Stage counts are unpublished, so the row is ordered by event, not by cycle. The allocation and release points are what the window measurements pin down.
each bar is one resource, taken where it starts and given back where it ends
taken at rename; a memory op opens a group, a branch closes it
one per register writing uop; freed when its map history retires
new register at rename; the old one freed at map history retire
held until a scheduler queue has room; one uop per queue per clk
held until the operands are ready and the uop is selected
taken at issue, not dispatch; loads and plain stores give it back before retire
written after the retire group commits
The early release of load and store queue entries, and the issue time allocation point, are why the same filler gives different window knees under a cache miss and under an ALU delay.
